**Finding: Deviation (high severity) — § 12.4**

§ 12.4 imposes on us a worldwide non-compete covering any product or service that competes with Copperleaf, running through the term plus 24 months. That breaches the walk-away threshold on two counts: an undefined scope ("any product or service that competes") and a post-term tail exceeding 12 months. It also flatly contradicts our protective § 12.3, in which Copperleaf acknowledges we have made no exclusivity or non-compete commitment.

**Redline (validated, preferred level):** delete § 12.4 in full, leaving § 12.3 to govern.

**Comment delivered:** "[Playbook] We cannot accept restrictions on the businesses we operate or the products we develop, buy or sell, so we have deleted the 24-month worldwide non-compete in § 12.4, which also directly contradicts § 12.3. If Copperleaf needs protection, we could consider a narrow alternative limited to a single named competing product during the term only (max 12 months), with carve-outs for internal development and acquisitions."

No other restrictive covenants binding us appeared in the document; restrictions running against Copperleaf are unaffected.
